purpose: Evaluate deep learning approaches for predicting TF-DNA binding plausibility

boltz2_200bp.verdict: No signal — scores cluster 0.28-0.44 regardless of true binding

boltz2_500bp.verdict: No signal — random pairs score slightly higher than known bindings

msa_boltz2.verdict: No signal — ColabFold has zero plant protein MSA coverage; scores identical to plain Boltz-2

enformer.model: Enformer (DeepMind, via TF Hub, GPU RTX 5070 Ti)

pilot_n20.note: Initial pilot with duplicate-target bug — superseded by large-scale validation
caveats: Negative controls had duplicate targets (TBXAS1/HSD11B2 reused)

large_scale_validation.verdict: Weak overall signal (AUC=0.518) — far weaker than the n=20 pilot suggested (+2.61 shrinks to +0.84). Signal is TF-specific and noisy with most TFs having only 1+1 edges. Not reliable as a global binding discriminator.

caveats: Human-only — no plant TF ChIP tracks in Enformer
27% of edges failed DNA sequence fetch (Ensembl REST errors)
Most TFs have only 1 positive + 1 negative — insufficient for per-TF AUC
Pilot n=20 AUC was inflated by duplicate-target bug and small sample

evo2.verdict: No signal — mean logit scores indistinguishable between positive and negative controls

evo2_sae.model: Evo2-7B + Goodfire SAE (layer 26, BatchTopK sparse autoencoder)
evo2_sae.binding_verdict: No signal for TF-DNA binding specificity

activator_vs_repressor.conclusion: Definitively no regulatory sign signal in promoter sequence

small_sample_inflation.note: n=20 inflated AUC and effect sizes dramatically; n=100 is authoritative

small_scale_diagnostics.note: Initial results at n=20 per class — superseded by large-scale validation above

evo2_sae.key_finding: The SAE is a phylogenomic composition encoder. Region discrimination follows a dicot > monocot > mammal gradient (arabidopsis AUC=0.889, potato 0.763, rice 0.636, human 0.545, mouse 0.500). Cross-species discrimination scales with evolutionary distance (all cross-kingdom=1.0, within-dicot=0.906, within-mammal=0.774). Zero encoding of regulatory function (activator/repressor AUC=0.506 at n=50+50). The Goodfire SAE learned plant genomic structure preferentially.
caveats: SAE was trained on mixed genomic data — encodes general genomic features, not regulatory specificity
Region discrimination is plant-biased: strong for dicots, weak-to-absent for mammals
C-sweep is critical: C≤0.01 zeros all coefficients in 32K-feature space; C=0.1 optimal for n=200
Small samples (n=20) inflate AUC and Cohen's d dramatically — always use n≥100
Activator/repressor result confirms regulatory sign depends on TF-DNA interaction context, not promoter sequence alone
DAP-seq binding sites have same SAE signature as random intergenic — the SAE does not see motifs

boltz2_large_scale.verdict: Definitively no binding signal across two species (n=50+50 each). Confirms n=20 pilot findings at scale.

jaspar_calibration.method: Best motif hit -log10(p_value) in target promoter; positive=measured interactions, negative=random genes

arabidopsis.verdict: STRONG — motif presence is highly discriminative; 59% hit rate in real targets vs 0.2% in random

petunia.verdict: STRONG — cross-species motif scanning works well

tomato.verdict: No hits in DB — motif scanning table may be incomplete for SL4.0

jaspar_calibration.verdict: JASPAR is the best binding discriminator for plant species. Arabidopsis AUC=0.795 with dramatic hit rate separation (59.4% vs 0.2%). Petunia AUC=0.715. Tomato motif_hits table appears empty.

deepbind.verdict: Dead end — model files on sandbox.zenodo.org return 404

evo2_linear_probe.model: Evo2-40B layer-26 mean-pooled hidden states + L1 logistic regression

negative_controls.source: random TF-gene pairs excluding all known edges

evo2_linear_probe.verdict: NO SIGNAL — AUC=0.50 across all regularization strengths. At strong regularization (C≤0.01) all coefficients are exactly zero; at weak regularization (C≥0.1) the probe overfits to noise (AUC<0.50). Zero of 8192 features carry binding-discriminative information.
caveats: 152 positive controls (37% of direct_signed edges skipped due to missing promoter DNA)
250 negative controls with near-100% DNA availability
Mean-pooling across 200bp sequence positions may lose positional binding signal
Only tested layer 26; other layers untested but unlikely to differ given SAE results

borzoi.approach: ChIP-seq track signal at TSS center bins (±1 bin around center_bin=3072)
borzoi.verdict: Chance level (AUC=0.509) — no improvement over Enformer despite 524K bp context

deeptfbs.approach: Per-TF transfer-learned model from DAP-seq, single sigmoid binding probability
deeptfbs.verdict: Below chance (AUC=0.358) — anti-discriminates. DAP-seq in vitro training doesn't predict in vivo regulatory edges

agront.approach: L1 logistic probe on mean-pooled last-hidden-state embeddings
agront.verdict: Weak signal (CV-AUC=0.594) with massive overfitting (train=0.999). Not generalizable

jaspar_bpnet.verdict: Not testable — CWMs (contribution weight matrices) not runnable neural networks. REST API returns 0 results for collection=deep_learning

plantcaduceus.verdict: Abandoned — requires mamba_ssm which cannot compile on CUDA 13.0/compute 12.0

conclusion: Large-scale validation (n=50+50 per condition, multiple species) substantially revised the initial n=20 findings. JASPAR motif scanning is the strongest binding discriminator (arabidopsis AUC=0.795, petunia 0.715). Enformer shows only weak overall signal at scale (AUC=0.518, down from pilot's 0.608 which had duplicate-target bug) — signal is real but TF-specific and noisy. Boltz-2 confirmed uninformative across both arabidopsis (AUC=0.420) and human (AUC=0.520). Evo2 (all variants: raw logits, SAE, linear probe) uninformative for binding. The Evo2 SAE is a phylogenomic composition encoder with dicot > monocot > mammal gradient. DeepBind inaccessible.
recommendation: For TF-DNA binding prediction: (1) JASPAR motif scanning is the primary tool for plant species — fast, database-driven, AUC=0.795. (2) Enformer provides weak supplementary signal for human TFs with strong ChIP-seq coverage, but should not be used as a global discriminator. (3) Boltz-2 and Evo2 approaches should not be used for binding prediction. The Evo2 SAE remains useful as a plant DNA region quality filter (arabidopsis AUC=0.889 for promoter vs coding). Regulatory sign cannot be predicted from promoter sequence alone — requires perturbation data.
